question.html:
A flywheel is a rotating cylinder used to store rotational kinetic energy. Energy can be transferred from the flywheel as it slows down.

A flywheel used to store energy has a moment of inertia of 0.072 kg m2 and a maximum angular speed of 8400 rad s−1.

a The rotational speed of the flywheel is reduced uniformly from the maximum speed to 3600 rad s−1 in a time of 9.6 s.

a.i Show that an average power of about 200 kW is transferred from the flywheel as its speed is reduced. [2]

a.ii Calculate the torque acting on the flywheel as it decelerates. [2]

a.iii Calculate the number of revolutions that the flywheel makes as it slows down. [2]

b

An engineer changes the flywheel design to increase the maximum energy that it can store.

Identify two factors that the engineer can change to do this.

[2]
